title: Molecular Comparability of Biomass-Derived Dextran for High-Value Functional Materials
content: Dextran production from sucrose-rich biomass offers opportunities for material valorization, but feedstock provenance does not establish molecular equivalence or explain downstream performance. This review examines how enzyme selectivity, recovery procedures, and reaction chemistry complicate comparisons between biomass-derived and reference dextrans. A targeted literature assessment, including studies published in 2025–2026, links glucosyl-transfer mechanisms and side-chain analysis to oxidation, methacrylation, and responsive-material formation. Three distinctions govern interpretation: substrate conversion differs from isolated polymer yield; an average molar mass or substitution value does not describe a molecular population; and functionality detected by an assay need not equal functionality accessible during material formation. Recent enzymatic studies demonstrate enzyme-dependent changes in polymer architecture and molar-mass distribution, whereas chemical studies reveal assay-dependent carbonyl accessibility and condition-dependent degradation. A framework is proposed for matched-feedstock experiments, fraction recovery, impurity depletion and reconstitution, and application-specific equivalence testing. Regenerative matrices, responsive carriers, and coating formulations illustrate proposed applications of this framework. The central conclusion is that biomass valorization becomes chemically interpretable when provenance, molecular structure, analytical response, and functional causality are evaluated separately and then connected by controlled comparisons.
